title: Connection churn causing tenant 5xx cascades — implement annealed retry and per-tenant inflight cap
creator: Miguel Alvarez
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported correlated 5xx spikes during tenant surges. Investigation points to aggressive client-side retries + rapid connection churn causing upstream edge proxy queue saturation, which then cascaded into model-serving timeouts and 5xx responses. This ticket implements a multi-layer mitigation: (1) server-side annealed retry gating to suppress synchronized retry storms, (2) per-tenant inflight request caps to bound resource contention, and (3) token-bucket smoothing at the edge to absorb short bursts without hitting the model backend. Goal is to stop customer-visible 5xx waves and provide deterministic degradation rather than large outage windows.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-03: Oncall reported 5xx wave affecting three enterprise tenants between 02:10–02:25 UTC; spike correlated with tenant migration window.
2026-03-04: Traces show >70% of failed requests were fast-failed with upstream ELB queue full and TCP resets; connection counts per edge node increased 4x during window.
2026-03-05: Heap of SDK logs from customer A show clients retried with default exponential backoff starting at 100ms — led to synchronized hammering when initial calls timed out.
2026-03-06: Load test replayed tenant pattern — reproduces 5xx cascade when >200 concurrent clients retry aggressively; KV cache thrash observed and model RPC latencies >2s.

2026-03-10: Root cause hypothesis: combination of (a) short client retry timers, (b) edge proxy connection churn losing warm keepalives, (c) absence of tenant-bounded inflight limits in the edge runtime.
2026-03-12: Confirmed mitigation knobs in staging: inflight cap + annealed retry reduced 5xx rate by 88% under synthetic replay (see metrics dashboard link in comments).
proposed_solution: 1) Implement server-side "annealed retries" controller: on first failure for a tenant, mark them into a decay window where retry acceptance rate is throttled and backoff windows are probabilistically randomized to avoid sync. 2) Add per-tenant inflight_request_cap with soft and hard thresholds (configurable): soft triggers emit WARN and begin probabilistic drop/fallback; hard threshold fast-fails new requests with 429. 3) Token-bucket smoothing at the edge (short window) to absorb microbursts and keep backend RPC Q depth below critical. 4) SDK guidance: recommend increasing client initial backoff and jitter in our public SDKs and add client-side opt-in to respect server-provided Retry-Delay header. 5) Observability: add tenant-level inflight gauges, retry-rate histograms, and a synthetic slow-path health-check to detect warming failures. 6) Canary + progressive rollout with per-tenant overrides for strategic customers.
acceptance_criteria: Reduced customer-visible 5xx rate by >=80% under production-like tenant surge replay (validated in staging)
No regression of P95 latency beyond 15% for normal traffic profiles
Per-tenant inflight cap config exists and can be toggled via console and API
SDKs honor Retry-Delay header and doc updates published
Playbook and runbook updated; oncall runbook points to new metrics and rollback steps
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy annealed-retry + inflight cap to staging; run replay for affected tenant patterns (owner: Priya)
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of hosted edge nodes and one low-risk tenant; collect 48h metrics and SLOs (owner: Jonah)
Phase 3 (regional ramp): expand to 25% then 75% with 24h observation windows; runbook triggers for rollback at defined thresholds
Phase 4 (global): enable by default with per-tenant overrides and console controls; announce SDK guidance and set client libraries to respect server signals
Rollback strategy: revert runtime flag, disable inflight cap, and set retry controller to pass-through; communicate to customers via status page and account owners
related_incidents: INC-2026-02-18-02: Tenant migration burst leading to degraded latency
out_of_scope: Model-level kernel optimizations (handled by runtime perf team separately)
Dedicated/Private deployment codepaths changes — this ticket targets Hosted edge/runtime only
postmortem_notes: Plan to run a full postmortem after global rollout, including customer communication timeline and SLA impact calculation
We will collect replay inputs from top-5 affected tenants to create long-term synthetic tests to catch regressions
Action item: revisit SDK defaults and release minor versions with safer backoff defaults within two weeks of rollout
